request.system:
You are the Extractor agent in a newsroom verification pipeline. You read one SEC filing
document and record what the employer itself says about job cuts and AI. You record claims only.
You never infer causation, never paraphrase quotes and never use a reporter's or analyst's framing.

Attribution labels (they describe what the EMPLOYER SAYS, never what is true):
- explicit: the employer's own words say AI, automation or machine learning is a reason for THESE job cuts
  (e.g. "we are reducing roles as AI now handles this work").
- partial: the employer mentions AI/automation in the same announcement as the cuts (strategy, reinvestment,
  "shifting resources to AI") but does not say AI caused the cuts.
- none: the employer announces cuts and does not connect them to AI or automation.

Return ONE JSON object with exactly these keys:
{
  "is_workforce_reduction": true | false,      // does the document announce job cuts / layoffs / a reduction in force?
  "company": string,                          // the employer's name as written in the document
  "event_date": "YYYY-MM-DD" | null,          // date of the announcement or of the cuts, if stated
  "jobs_cut": integer | null,                 // number of positions cut, ONLY if the document states a number
  "jobs_cut_text": string | null,             // the exact words stating the number or percentage, copied verbatim
  "cut_quote": string | null,                 // the one sentence, copied VERBATIM, in which the document announces or
                                              // reports the job cuts; null when is_workforce_reduction is false
  "ai_attribution": "explicit" | "partial" | "none",
  "ai_quote": string | null,                  // 1-2 sentences copied VERBATIM (character for character) in which the
                                              // employer connects the cuts to AI/automation; null when attribution is none
  "notes": string                             // one short sentence on anything ambiguous
}
is_workforce_reduction is true ONLY when the document itself announces or reports job cuts. Mentions inside
forward-looking-statement disclaimers, risk-factor lists or legal boilerplate (e.g. "the effectiveness of our
restructuring and workforce reduction program", "artificial intelligence laws") do NOT count, and an AI quote must never
come from that boilerplate.
Copy quotes exactly as they appear, including punctuation. If the document states a percentage but no headcount,
set jobs_cut to null and put the percentage wording in jobs_cut_text. Output JSON only.

<<<
AI model architecture has been built and trained across an in-house dataset and demonstrated the ability to screen candidates, with initial Optimer® candidates currently being validated.

The Group has purchased and deployed new automation machinery to expand binder development and manufacturing capacity, supporting revenue growth well beyond the level required for breakeven.

"Following April's fundraise, we have used the proceeds to build the foundations for the next phase of growth. Our AI programme has progressed from a standing start to candidate validation in a matter of months, our manufacturing capacity has been expanded to support partners at commercial scale, and we are now building a therapeutic pipeline spanning RNAi delivery to multiple diseases and organs including fibrosis and kidney, along with radiopharmaceuticals.

Aptamer is strategically focused on two of the most significant challenges in modern drug development: targeting "undruggable" proteins and enabling delivery of therapeutics to tissues beyond the liver. Its proprietary Optimer® platform, supported by more than 15 years of discovery data and an expanding AI-enabled discovery engine, is designed to accelerate the identification of high-quality binders against challenging biological targets.

We are pleased to report a successful year for Aptamer, where we have seen continued growth, marked by initial assets being out-licensed and delivering revenue, an increase in fee-for-service revenue driven by repeat business from large pharmaceutical companies, and, following the fundraise in April 2026, investment in artificial intelligence (AI), manufacturing capacity, and initiation of our own therapeutic pipeline.

Increased capacity and machine learning advances

The £4.1 million of net proceeds raised in April 2026 was sought to expand manufacturing capability, fund the AI programme, develop Optimers for a range of therapeutic targets and advance Optimer® candidates through preclinical studies.

New automation machinery was purchased during the period, which will improve the efficiency of development programmes, and add manufacturing capacity to support out-licensed assets for our partners to deliver commercial volumes for their products. We have also refined the discovery process itself, delivering a 50% increase in speed for each discovery round. Alongside this, laboratory processes for conjugation have been standardised, broadening the range of functional groups that can be added to Optimer® binders in-house, bringing work previously carried out by external partners in-house and shortening development timelines.

The artificial intelligence programme has advanced rapidly since initiation in April 2026. We have built and trained a model architecture on our discovery dataset, accumulated over years of laboratory work, and shown it can screen candidates in silico. The first Optimer® candidates produced by the model are now being validated in the laboratory ahead of an initial service launch. If validation is successful, this will enable improved customer discovery with faster timelines and support in-house development programmes.

With two royalty-bearing licensing agreements now signed and further parties in discussion, a sales pipeline that has expanded to £7.0 million, and a therapeutic pipeline spanning fibrotic disease, kidney and brain delivery, and radiopharmaceuticals now underway, Aptamer enters the new financial year with a materially different business than it had twelve months ago. Fee-for-service and repeating demand from the world's largest pharmaceutical companies continues to broaden, our capacity to meet that demand has been expanded through new automation, and a therapeutic pipeline spanning fibrotic disease, kidney and brain delivery, and radiopharmaceuticals is now underway.

The AI programme adds a further dimension to this growth. As the model moves from validation into service, we expect it to shorten discovery timelines for our partners in the near term and support the design of entirely new Optimer® sequences in the longer term, improving the platform’s speed and economics and broadening its target potential.

In addition, these funds are allowing the Group to develop our own AI platform offering, with the ambition of being able to improve the Group’s discovery service offering.
